subject: business-studies
title: Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet
welcome_lead: Read the two core financial statements like a CFO.
meta_desc: A-Level Finance: income statement (P&L) and statement of financial position.
final_note: Profit measures performance over a period; the balance sheet shows position on a date.

concepts.def: Income from sales over a period.
Resources the business owns or controls.
Owner's claim on the business: assets minus liabilities.

walkthroughs.body_html: The P&L runs from revenue down to net profit: deduct cost of sales for gross profit, deduct operating expenses for operating profit, deduct interest and tax for net profit.
The balance sheet on a single date lists non-current and current assets, current and non-current liabilities, and equity. By definition assets equal liabilities plus equity.
Firms can manipulate the balance sheet at year-end - paying suppliers early, delaying invoices - to flatter ratios. Analysts use multi-year trends to detect window dressing.
